_howto: site holds global values used on every page. gbpUrl is the Google Business Profile link: leave it empty and the footer/contact GBP link is omitted everywhere, set it once and it renders site wide. Use the real share link from the GBP dashboard (g.page/... or maps.app.goo.gl/...), never a google.com/search URL. Each city needs city, areas (real neighborhoods, verified), and intro (2 to 3 sentences, unique voice per city, no shared sentence structure). Brand rules apply: Alexa only, no banned terms, no em dashes, no hyphens between words, no pricing.

cities.areas: Eagle Trace, the Country Club neighborhoods, and the Coral Springs side of Heron Bay
cities.intro: Eagle Trace wraps its homes around a private golf course, the Country Club streets nearby run to comfortable single family houses, and Heron Bay reaches across the line into Parkland. That is three different kinds of home in one city, and they do not take the same plan. We walk your rooms as they actually are and build the Alexa floor plan from that.

cities.areas: Boca West, Boca Del Mar, and East Boca
cities.intro: Ask what a Boca Raton home looks like and you will get five answers. Country club estates in Boca West, family houses through Boca Del Mar, and the older low slung streets of East Boca near the water are not the same project, and we do not plan them as though they were.

cities.areas: MiraLago, Cascata, and Parkland Golf and Country Club
cities.intro: Most of Parkland is newer construction and it shows. MiraLago and Cascata went up from 2014 onward, one and two story estate homes with two and three car garages, and Parkland Golf and Country Club is still adding to the inventory. Bigger footprints mean more rooms that have to work together, which is the part the floor plan settles before anyone picks up a drill.

cities.areas: Palm Aire, Cypress Bend, and the Old Pompano beachside streets
cities.intro: Pompano splits fairly cleanly between condo living and canal living. Cypress Bend and the rest of Palm Aire are mid rise and high rise units where the work stays inside the walls you own, while the older streets near Old Pompano and the beach are single family houses with wiring of their own. Your plan gets written for whichever of those two you are actually in.

cities.areas: Wynmoor, Winston Park, and Regency Lakes
cities.intro: Wynmoor on its own is more than five thousand condos spread across a hundred and thirty odd mid rise buildings, all of it 55 and over. Cross a couple of roads into Winston Park or Regency Lakes and you are in single family territory instead. Same city, two completely different starting points, so we begin by asking which one is yours.

cities.areas: The Cove, Deer Creek, and Century Village
cities.intro: The Cove sits on the Intracoastal, Deer Creek sits on a golf course, and Century Village is low maintenance condo living. What works beautifully in one of those is wrong in the next. We plan room by room, inside your home, before a single device gets ordered.

cities.areas: Lake Ida, the Atlantic Avenue corridor, and Delray Lakes
cities.intro: Lake Ida is the giveaway that Delray is older than it looks. Its streets still hold 1950s Florida ranch bungalows sitting next to Key West style rebuilds and the occasional modern estate, which is a polite way of saying the wiring behind the walls varies enormously from house to house. We find out what is actually there before the plan promises you anything.

cities.areas: Hunters Run, Canyon Lakes, and Renaissance Commons
cities.intro: Hunters Run runs to twenty three separate subcommunities behind the one gate, mixing single family homes, attached villas, and condos. West of there Canyon Lakes is newer gated construction, and Renaissance Commons is townhomes and low rise buildings on the old mall site. A plan that suits one of those three will not suit the other two.

cities.areas: Victoria Park, Coral Ridge, and Harbor Beach
cities.intro: Coral Ridge and Harbor Beach are deep water addresses where the house was more or less built around the dock. Victoria Park is a different animal again: midcentury ranch houses, restored older homes, and newer townhomes turning up on the same block. We plan for the house in front of us rather than the postcode.

cities.areas: Weston Hills, Savanna, and The Ridges
cities.intro: Weston was planned to the inch and the housing follows suit. Savanna runs one and two story homes around a chain of lakes, The Ridges leans Mediterranean with townhomes folded in among the houses, and Weston Hills has been golf course living since 1993. Each of those gets its own Alexa floor plan, never a shared one.

cities.areas: Plantation Acres, Jacaranda, and Hawks Landing
cities.intro: Plantation Acres is the outlier, with lots running one to four acres and horses still permitted on them. The rest of the city is more familiar ground: midcentury ranch houses through the older sections, Jacaranda mixing single family with townhomes and condos, Hawks Landing gated and custom built. An acreage property and a townhome need very different plans, and we draw both.

cities.areas: Venetian Isles, Coral Key Villas, and the Hillsboro Inlet waterfront
cities.intro: Nearly every street in Lighthouse Point ends at water. Venetian Isles is canal frontage with a straight run out through the Hillsboro Inlet, Coral Key Villas is largely one story, and the city as a whole is single family with almost no towers in it. Waterfront houses come with their own quirks and we plan around them instead of pretending otherwise.

cities.areas: Paradise Gardens, Holiday Springs, and Oriole Gardens
cities.intro: Margate does a great deal of one story living. Paradise Gardens holds over a thousand single story homes across four subdivisions, each with its own clubhouse and its own board, while Holiday Springs wraps six developments of Spanish style houses, condos, and townhomes around a former golf course. One floor changes how a plan gets drawn, and usually for the better.

cities.areas: Kings Point, the Mainlands, and The Woodlands
cities.intro: Kings Point is the big one: close to five thousand condos, villas, and two story coach homes, all resale, all 55 and over. The Mainlands is single family in much the same active adult spirit, and The Woodlands mixes houses with townhomes under some genuinely old trees. We plan for the one you live in, at whatever pace suits you.

cities.areas: Welleby, Sunrise Lakes, and the Sawgrass corridor
cities.intro: Welleby is the shorthand most people reach for when they talk about living in Sunrise, and it is genuinely mixed: single family houses on some streets, condo buildings on others, the park sitting in the middle of it. Sunrise Lakes adds a good deal more condo stock again. Whether your project is one unit or a whole house shapes the plan more than anything else will.

cities.areas: Long Lake Ranches, Forest Ridge, and the western horse country
cities.intro: Davie still lets horses use the road, which tells you most of what you need to know about the western half of town. Long Lake Ranches puts custom estates on half acre and larger lots out that way, while Forest Ridge runs smaller and closer in, from single family houses down to townhomes. Big house or small, the plan is drawn to the rooms you actually have.

cities.areas: SilverLakes, Chapel Trail, and Grand Palms
cities.intro: Pembroke Pines is master planned country and the plans are enormous. Chapel Trail alone runs past two thousand five hundred homes with a nature preserve attached, SilverLakes gathers thirty nine communities under a single association, and Grand Palms threads its houses along a golf course. Identical on paper, quite different once you are inside, which is why we measure yours.

cities.areas: Rock Creek, Embassy Lakes, and Monterra
cities.intro: Rock Creek was the first master planned corner of Cooper City and roughly thirty years of building shows in it, from midcentury ranch houses in some of the twelve subdivisions to two story Spanish Revivals in others. Embassy Lakes and Monterra arrived later and newer. The age of the house tends to drive the plan far more than the address does.

cities.areas: North Andrews Gardens, Lloyd Estates, and Coral Heights
cities.intro: Drive North Andrews Gardens and you are looking at early 1950s housing built for returning veterans, one story ranches mostly running between twelve hundred and sixteen hundred square feet. Lloyd Estates nearby kept the single floor idea and put it on larger lots. Compact older homes make some of the most satisfying Alexa floor plans we draw, because nothing in them goes to waste.

cities.areas: Coral Gardens, the Middle River waterfront, and the Wilton Drive district
cities.intro: The Middle River loops right the way around Wilton Manors, which is how it picked up the Island City name. Inside that loop sits mostly 1950s and 1960s ranch houses and wood cottages, with Coral Gardens running along the north fork and a handful of waterfront Mediterranean homes mixed in. Older wiring in a compact home is a combination we work with constantly.
